podcast.title: Critic Robert Hull's Disparaging Remarks (1975)
podcast.body: In a misogynistic assessment from 1975, critic Robert Hull crudely dismissed Susie Quatro with the comment "She'd Stomp You in Your Marbles" in a crude ranking of female singers he would like "to sit in your lap." "Susie Quattro, She'd Stomp You in Your Marbles."

podcast.title: Times Square Soundtrack Contribution (1980)
podcast.body: Suzi Quatro contributed to the soundtrack for the 1980 movie *Time Square*. This soundtrack was significant for being among the earliest compilations to feature the nascent alternative music of the day, which included punk rock and new wave. "There was Lou Reed and the Cure and Patty Smith and Susie Quattro."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: "Happy Days" Role as Leather Tuscadero
podcast.body: For many in North America, Suzi Quatro is best recognized for her role as Leather Tuscadero, Fonzie's girlfriend, on the popular old television show "Happy Days." This acting credit contrasts sharply with her musical fame elsewhere. "Remember, Fawzi's girlfriend, Leather Tuscadero? Yeah, that was Susie Quattro."

podcast.title: Acting Role on Happy Days
podcast.body: In North America, Suzi Quatro is perhaps most recognized for her acting role as Leather Tuscadero, Fonzie's girlfriend, on the popular old show *Happy Days*. "Remember, Fanzi's girlfriend, Leather Tuske-Darrow? Yeah, that was Susie Quattro."

podcast.title: Family Connection to Fanny
podcast.body: Suzi Quatro is the sister of Patty Quatro, who joined the band Fanny in 1974. "She had a sister named Susie, and Susie became a big deal in the UK, Europe, and Australia."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: Global Success vs. North American Obscurity
podcast.body: Suzi Quatro achieved massive success in the UK, Europe, and Australia, selling over 50 million albums worldwide. However, she remains relatively unknown in North America, never reaching the same level of stardom there as she did elsewhere. "But never in North America, where she still isn't that well known, which is crazy since she sold over 50 million albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

podcast.title: International Star, North American Obscurity
podcast.body: Suzi Quatro, sister of Fanny's Patty Quatro, achieved massive success in the UK, Europe, and Australia, selling over 50 million albums worldwide. Despite these staggering sales, she remains relatively unknown in North America, where she never attained the same star status. "She had a sister named Susie, and Susie became a big deal in the UK, Europe, and Australia, but never in North America, where she still isn't that well known, which is crazy since she sold over 50 million albums."

srcs.source: The Ongoing History of New Music

xref.title: Detroit-based Female Drummer
xref.body: Nancy Ball played drums with The Pleasure Seekers, a Detroit-based all-girl band. This group is also notable for featuring Suzi Quatro, who would later become a significant rock star. "Then there was Nancy Ball who played drums with the pleasure seekers that have Detroit. And yes, that's the same group that gave his future star, Susie Quattro."
